question: Both Calore, Cholis and Weniger (arXiv:1409.0042v1) and the Fermi-LAT Collaboration (arXiv:1704.03910v2) estimate how well the Galactic diffuse emission is modeled by fitting a dark-matter-like template in control regions along the Galactic plane, away from the Galactic Center. For each paper: at which longitudes is the template placed, and how are the results of these fits turned into a systematic uncertainty for the Galactic Center? For arXiv:1409.0042v1, also give the number of overlapping regions in which the template is fitted (the one centred on the Galactic Center included) and the number that enters the uncertainty estimate.

arguments.answer:
Calore, Cholis & Weniger (1409.0042v1): The GCE template is moved along the disk in 5° steps, centred at ℓ = k·5° with k = −14,…,14. Each position has its own ROI, (−20°+5k)° ≤ ℓ ≤ (20°+5k)° and 2° ≤ |b| ≤ 20°. That gives 29 overlapping ROIs, including the GC one. Only 22 enter the uncertainty estimate, those with 20° ≤ |ℓ| ≤ 70°. The flux absorbed by the template in each of these 22 ROIs is the residual. Its covariance matrix across energy bins (mean and scatter over the 22 ROIs) is the empirical model systematic used at the GC. For the GCE spectral fits this matrix is truncated to its first three principal components, to avoid double-counting statistical errors.

Fermi-LAT (1704.03910v2): The gNFW template is shifted in 10° steps in longitude at b = 0°, over 30° ≤ l ≤ 330°, with an all-sky fit at each position. In each fit the best-fit DM-like signal is expressed as a fraction of the effective background, f = N_sig/b_eff. δf_GP is the value of f exceeded in only 16% of the control-region fits, a one-sided 1σ level. This is adopted as the systematic fraction, δf_syst = δf_GP. The systematic uncertainty at the GC is δN_sig,syst = b_eff × δf_syst.
